text: Study loan repayments are collected through the tax system once repayment income exceeds the threshold.
Taxpayers may object to an amended assessment within the prescribed objection period.
Dispute resolution clauses in awards require matters to be discussed first at the workplace level.
ASIC requires registered entities to review annual company statements and pay the annual review fee within sixty days.
The Small Business Fair Dismissal Code applies to employers with fewer than fifteen employees.
Australian financial services licensees must act efficiently, honestly and fairly.
Full-time employees receive ten days of paid personal or carer's leave for each year of service.
Employees covered by an award must be paid at least the minimum rates for their classification level.
Whistleblower protections apply to eligible disclosures about misconduct within a regulated entity.
Market manipulation and insider trading are serious offences under the Corporations Act.
Termination notice must be in writing and specify the day the employment ends.
The ASX Corporate Governance Principles operate on an if not, why not disclosure basis.
Every Australian company director must hold a verified 15-digit Director ID issued by the Australian Business Registry Services.
Rental property owners can deduct interest on loans used to purchase an income-producing property.
Minutes of directors' and members' meetings must be recorded within one month.
Businesses with a GST turnover of $75,000 or more must register for goods and services tax.
Substantial holding notices must be lodged when a person acquires a voting interest of 5 percent or more.
Fringe benefits tax is payable by employers on non-cash benefits such as private use of a company car.
Public holidays allow employees to be absent on the day without loss of pay for ordinary hours.
Concessional superannuation contributions are taxed at 15 percent within the fund up to the annual cap.
The Fair Work Ombudsman may issue compliance notices requiring employers to rectify underpayments.
Division 293 tax imposes an additional 15 percent on concessional contributions for very high-income earners.
Superannuation contributions must be paid quarterly by the required cutoff dates to comply with super guarantee legislation.
A special resolution requires at least 75 percent of the votes cast by members entitled to vote.
Compassionate leave of two days is available when a member of an employee's immediate family dies.
Workers compensation insurance must be held by employers to cover work-related injuries.
Withholding tax applies to interest, dividends and royalties paid to non-resident recipients.
Section 100A can apply to reimbursement agreements involving trust distributions to low-tax beneficiaries.
Casual loading is paid to casual staff at a default rate of 25 percent in lieu of paid leave entitlements.
The replaceable rules govern internal management for companies that do not adopt their own constitution.
Section 180 of the Corporations Act mandates that directors exercise their powers and discharge duties with care and diligence.
Apprentices and trainees are paid according to their year of training and qualification level.
Registered schemes must have a responsible entity that is a public company holding a financial services licence.
Takeover bids for listed companies above the 20 percent threshold must comply with Chapter 6.
Right of entry permits allow union officials to enter workplaces to investigate suspected contraventions.
Long service leave entitlements are generally governed by state and territory legislation.
Individuals must lodge their income tax return by 31 October unless they use a registered tax agent.
Fuel tax credits refund excise included in fuel used in eligible business activities.
Pay secrecy clauses in employment contracts are no longer enforceable.
Trust beneficiaries are assessed on their share of the net income of the trust estate.
The general anti-avoidance rule in Part IVA cancels tax benefits obtained through schemes entered for the dominant purpose of avoiding tax.
Financial reports must give a true and fair view of the financial position and performance of the entity.
